evidence.quote: Fourteen patients with type 2 diabetes (56±2 years) wore a CGMS during 3 days.
Participants randomly performed AER and COMB sessions, both in the morning (24 h after CGMS placement), and at least 7 days apart.

Glucose variability was evaluated by glucose standard deviation, glucose variance, mean amplitude of glycemic excursions (MAGE), and glucose coefficient of variation (conventional methods) as well as by spectral and symbolic analysis (non-conventional methods).
Glucose levels decreased immediately after AER and COMB protocols by ∼16%, which was sustained for approximately 3 hours.
Comparing the two exercise modalities, responses over a 24-h period after the sessions were similar for glucose levels, glucose variance and glucose coefficient of variation.

answer_components.answer: The 2013 aerobic versus combined exercise trial studied fourteen patients with type 2 diabetes (56±2 years) who wore a continuous glucose monitoring system (CGMS) during 3 days and randomly performed aerobic (AER) and combined (COMB) exercise sessions, both in the morning 24 h after CGMS placement and at least 7 days apart; the trial measured glucose variability using glucose standard deviation, glucose variance, mean amplitude of glycemic excursions (MAGE) and glucose coefficient of variation (conventional methods) as well as spectral and symbolic analysis (non-conventional methods) [PMC:PMC3594238]. In that trial, glucose levels decreased immediately after both the AER and COMB protocols by approximately 16%, a reduction sustained for approximately 3 hours, and over the 24-h period after the sessions the two exercise modalities showed similar responses for glucose levels, glucose variance and glucose coefficient of variation [PMC:PMC3594238].

answer_components.answer: In the 2016 brown-rice-based vegan diet randomized trial in Korean adults with type 2 diabetes, mean HbA1c levels at weeks 0, 4 and 12 were 7.7%, 7.2% and 7.1% in the vegan diet group and 7.4%, 7.2% and 7.2% in the conventional diet group [PMC:PMC4890770]. Both the vegan and conventional diet groups showed significant reductions in HbA1c over the 12 weeks, but the reduction was larger with the vegan diet than with the conventional diet (-0.5% vs. -0.2%; p-for-interaction = 0.017) [PMC:PMC4890770]. Among participants with high compliance only, the between-group difference in HbA1c reduction was larger still, at -0.9% for the vegan group versus -0.3% for the conventional group [PMC:PMC4890770].

chunks.title: Effect of a Brown Rice Based Vegan Diet and Conventional Diabetic Diet on Glycemic Control of Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A 12-Week Randomized Clinical Trial
chunks.text: Several intervention studies have suggested that vegetarian or vegan diets have clinical benefits, particularly in terms of glycemic control, in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D); however, no randomized controlled trial has been conducted in Asians who more commonly depend on plant-based foods, as compared to Western populations. Here, we aimed to compare the effect of a vegan diet and conventional diabetic diet on glycemic control among Korean individuals.
